headline: CPI RUNS HOT — GOLD AND SILVER RALLY ANYWAY: 90% HIKE ODDS AND METALS STILL UP 1.5%
snippet: August CPI landed September 11 with core inflation at 0.3% for the month — a tenth above consensus — holding the annual core rate at 2.4%. The natural expectation: hot data cements rate-hike bets, gold falls. Instead, both metals climbed more than 1.5% at midday on CPI day, with gold recovering toward $4,380 and silver advancing in tandem despite Fed hike odds for the September 16 decision jumping to approximately 90% on CME FedWatch. GoldSilver.com's analysis identifies the disconnect: the market had already priced in the hike, and forward-looking positioning was focused on what comes after — the dot plot's signal, or a 'one-and-done' message from the Fed Chair. When bad news for metals is already in the price, the absence of an even-worse print becomes a catalyst to the upside. This is a meaningful shift from the PPI-day behaviour on Thursday, when silver fell three times harder than gold. The CPI data — mixed headline, hot core — created a different positioning dynamic: the hike is priced; what isn't priced is a clearly hawkish dot plot signalling multiple further hikes. For retail investors holding junior miners, the FOMC event itself may be less important than Powell's language about the path forward. A September hike framed as 'last for now' would be structurally bullish for the sector in the quarters that follow.

headline: $105 OIL AND RECORD DIESEL ARE SQUEEZING GOLD MINERS FROM BELOW EVEN AS GOLD HOLDS $4,348
snippet: SD Bullion's September 12 weekly market wrap identifies a threat to gold mining margins that is receiving far less attention than the headline gold price: crude oil above $105 per barrel and record diesel prices are inflating open-pit operating costs faster than sector models accounted for six months ago. While spot gold closed the week at approximately $4,348/oz and silver at $64.50 — both showing modest gains on Friday after Thursday's inflation-data selloff — the cost side of the miner equation is moving against producers. Diesel is the dominant variable cost in open-pit mining, powering haul trucks, excavators, and generators. In Africa and Latin America — where currency depreciation compounds the effect — the real cost per tonne moved is rising substantially. The GDX's August rally (+33%) priced in historically record revenue margins, but those margins were calculated against $70-$80/bbl oil; $105 oil is a different calculus entirely. SD Bullion also flags rising 10-year Treasury yields above 5.1% and sustained Fed rate-hike expectations as co-headwinds into Q4. For retail investors evaluating junior miners, the sector remains fundamentally attractive at record gold prices — but the diesel and energy cost trend warrants direct questions to management about operating cost guidance assumptions. Companies with underground resources or in jurisdictions with stable energy markets (Canada, Australia, Nevada) carry less exposure than open-pit operations in higher-risk energy regions.

headline: FIVE MARKET SIGNALS OUTSIDE THE GOLD PRICE ARE ALL POINTING THE SAME WAY INTO THIS WEEK'S FED MEETING
snippet: GoldSilver.com's FOMC week digest identifies five separate market signals — all outside the daily gold price tick — that were pointing toward a hard-assets bull setup heading into the September 15-16 Federal Reserve decision: (1) Options flow on gold contracts showing unusual call-side activity at strikes above $4,500 for November expiry; (2) Bloomberg Commodity Index crossing a key moving average, suggesting institutional rotation toward hard assets broadly; (3) A copper COMEX-vs-LME premium hitting a record — COMEX copper pricing significantly above LME — a setup historically associated with commodity re-pricing across the complex; (4) HSBC upgrading its Brent crude forecast to $112/bbl by December, based on Iran production disruption; and (5) COMEX data showing managed-money speculators cutting gold net-long positions for the fourth consecutive week — a positioning setup that historically precedes sharp short-squeeze rallies when a data point surprises to the upside. Fed rate-hike odds for September 16 swung from 54% to 26% to 58% in six weeks before settling near 90% after PPI, illustrating how volatile the probability has been. For junior mining investors, this five-signal convergence is the kind of setup that precedes sector-wide re-ratings — not in the immediate FOMC week, but typically 6-12 weeks after the Fed inflection creates clarity on the forward path.

headline: COPPER SNAPS 10-WEEK WIN STREAK ON TARIFF HESITATION — SHFE INVENTORIES HIT LOWEST SINCE JAN 2024
snippet: Copper posted its first weekly loss since June 2026 after a Reuters report indicated the White House had not yet determined its position on import tariffs for refined copper — removing the tariff-premium bid that had driven LME three-month copper to a record $14,875 per tonne on September 10. By Friday's close, the contract had fallen to $14,271, a 4% decline from the record. However, the underlying physical supply picture confirms the record was not purely speculative: Shanghai Futures Exchange copper inventories fell 13% in a single week to 54,780 tonnes — the lowest level since January 2024 — while LME available stocks stood at only 117,600 tonnes globally. The tariff question is deferred, not resolved: the White House is reportedly weighing manufacturing cost impacts against the domestic mining incentive. Once a decision is made in either direction, the premium or discount will be re-priced immediately. For TSX-V copper explorers and developers, the September volatility confirms the structural floor holds above $13,000/t even after the correction. Copper's 2026 pattern — record, correct, recover, record — reflects a commodity in genuine physical deficit, not one sustained by speculation alone.

headline: CHINA LITHIUM FUTURES CRASH 5% ON CATL PERMIT REVOCATION: ALBEMARLE -3.76%, SQM -3.60%
snippet: China's LC2701 lithium carbonate futures contract fell 4.99% to 134,800 CNY per tonne on September 11, 2026, as Chinese traders took profits following a dramatic price run linked to the ongoing closure of CATL's Jianxiawo mine — China's largest lithium operation by capacity, which remains on care and maintenance after Yichun regulators revoked the mine's environmental impact assessment acceptance. More than 70 formal complaints about an undisclosed tailings-pond dispute triggered the revocation; CATL's attempts to restart informally in July prompted the regulatory intervention. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence halved its 2026 Jianxiawo output forecast to 32,000 tonnes LCE from 62,500 tonnes — a 30,500-tonne supply gap in a global market already running its sixth consecutive annual deficit. The futures sell-off dragged US-listed producers: Albemarle closed at US$117.52, down 3.76%; Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile finished at US$69.88, down 3.60%. Physical battery-grade lithium carbonate in China's EXW market held at RMB 150,300-160,500/tonne, up 0.3% on the day, confirming the physical shortage is still present even as futures speculators book gains. Lithium is still +96% year-over-year despite the week's pullback. For investors in ASX and TSX-V hard-rock lithium developers — Pilbara, Core, Patriot, etc. — the Jianxiawo closure removes a major source of anticipated Chinese supply and strengthens the case for ex-China producers unaffected by Beijing's regulatory environment.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $90/LB INTO FOMC WEEK AS WORLD NUCLEAR BODY PROJECTS DEMAND MORE THAN DOUBLING BY 2040
snippet: Uranium spot dipped marginally to $90.15 per pound on September 11, down 0.06% on the day but still near multi-year highs, entering Federal Reserve decision week with unchanged structural fundamentals. The World Nuclear Association's World Nuclear Outlook 2026 report — published September 11 — projects global reactor requirements to more than double by 2040, driven by existing fleet life extensions, new-build programs in China, India, South Korea and Eastern Europe, and unprecedented demand from AI data-centre operators. The AI-to-nuclear nexus is moving from thesis to contract: Google's 22-year Finnish nuclear PPA (announced last week) demonstrates that Tier-1 hyperscalers are now making 20-year commitments to nuclear baseload power, creating a structural demand anchor that did not exist in prior demand models. With uranium term contract prices at 18-year highs near $96.50/lb, Cameco guiding to a 2026 production shortfall, and Kazatomprom having cut 2026 output by 10%, uranium's FOMC sensitivity is structurally lower than gold's: a rate hike does not reduce reactor fuel requirements. Crucially, the doubling-by-2040 WNA forecast means every Athabasca Basin, Namibian, and Kazakhstani development-stage project now has a 15-year demand signal that validates capex at $90+/lb uranium. The uranium thesis heading into September 2026 is rare in commodities: supply constrained, demand accelerating, and the price re-contracting cycle only partway through.

headline: $105 OIL, RISING YIELDS AND 90% HIKE BETS: THE THREE-HEADWIND SETUP RESHAPING GOLD'S Q4 2026 PATH
snippet: Limitless Metals' September 10 analysis frames gold's path into Q4 2026 as navigating three simultaneous macro headwinds that were absent when the year began: (1) Crude oil above $105/bbl driven by Iran conflict disruption, feeding headline inflation and keeping the Federal Reserve in a hiking posture rather than easing — each oil spike becomes a real-yield headwind for gold; (2) 10-year Treasury yields above 5.1%, directly competing with non-yielding gold for safe-haven capital allocation; and (3) September rate-hike odds climbing to 60-90% on CME FedWatch — a complete reversal from the January 2026 consensus that the Fed was effectively done tightening. The analysis notes that gold has outperformed most major asset classes despite these headwinds — holding above $4,200 even as yields, the dollar, and oil all moved against it — reflecting the durable floor provided by central bank buying (244 tonnes in Q1 2026), record ETF inflows, and de-dollarisation demand. The key Q4 setup: if the September 16 hike is framed as the last, all three headwinds ease simultaneously. If the dot plot signals further tightening, gold's $4,200 floor faces a genuine test. For retail investors holding junior gold miners, the position sizing question ahead of Tuesday is not just about direction — it is about the magnitude and language of the Fed's signal, which carries more weight than the rate decision itself.

headline: SITKA GOLD EXTENDS RHOSGOBEL 350m EAST IN YUKON: 159m AT 1.14 g/t Au WITH TUNGSTEN CRITICAL-MINERAL KICKER
snippet: Sitka Gold Corp. (TSXV: SIG) has extended the Rhosgobel deposit at its RC Gold Project in Yukon's Dawson Range approximately 350 metres to the east of the prior year's drilling boundary, per drill results covered by North of 60 Mining News on September 11. The headline intercept returned 159.2 metres at 1.14 g/t gold from surface — a wide-interval, bulk-tonnage result — within a larger envelope of 256.9 metres grading 0.84 g/t gold. A 7.3-metre sub-interval hit 8.89 g/t gold. The key discovery element: 13.9 metres of 0.383% tungsten trioxide (WO3) was also intersected, confirming the Rhosgobel system is a gold-tungsten deposit. Tungsten is a Canada-listed critical mineral with approximately 80% of global supply concentrated in China; a by-product tungsten credit at any material grade adds strategic-mineral value to a gold system that is already economically compelling at $4,300+/oz. Sitka's 60,000-metre 2026 drill program is approximately 75% complete, with the deposit confirmed open in multiple directions. The step-out east and the tungsten association together support a re-rating thesis: Rhosgobel is growing in both areal extent and commodity profile. For investors screening Yukon gold, the dual gold-tungsten nature of RC Gold gives Sitka a differentiated position among Dawson Range explorers.

headline: AMEX GOLD STRIKES ROSE ZONE AT PERRON, ABITIBI — NEW HIGH-GRADE DISCOVERY 165m BELOW WORKING MINE RAMP
snippet: Amex Gold Mining Inc. (TSXV: AMX) announced September 10 the discovery of a new gold zone — named the Rosé Zone — at the Perron Project in the northwestern Abitibi region of Quebec, located approximately 165 metres directly below the underground ramp currently being advanced for the ongoing bulk sample and planned mine access. The discovery is structurally significant because it lies beneath fully-financed infrastructure: underground drill access to test the Rosé Zone at depth will be available from existing development without additional capital. The deepest hole drilled into the zone (PE-26-950, 410 metres) returned visible gold and ended in mineralization, leaving the Rosé Zone open at depth. Early structural mapping indicates gold is hosted in tension veins branching from a larger structural corridor interpreted to also control the Alizée Zone to the north-northwest — meaning the Rosé and Alizée zones may share a common feeder, substantially increasing the system's resource potential. Perron hosts one of Quebec Abitibi's highest-grade near-surface gold resources, with a bulk sample program currently underway. A new high-grade zone confirmed open at depth below active mine development — with underground access imminent — is precisely the kind of result that extends resource life without greenfield exploration cost. At $4,348/oz gold, incremental high-grade discovery at an Abitibi project this close to production is a compelling risk-reward setup for TSX-V investors.

headline: TECTONIC METALS CONFIRMS 300m-DEEP HIGH-GRADE GOLD CORRIDOR AT FLAT GOLD, ALASKA — BULK-TONNAGE RIRGS THESIS SOLIDIFIES
snippet: Tectonic Metals Inc. (CVE: TECT) released September 10 the first assay results from 15 drill holes (2,276 metres) at Chicken Mountain — the most advanced intrusion target at its 99,840-acre Flat Gold Project in southwest Alaska. Hole CMD26-036 returned 1.40 g/t gold over 30.0 metres including 4.58 g/t Au over 4.50 metres, and intersected gold mineralization to 388 metres downhole — extending the higher-grade corridor to over 300 metres vertical depth in a zone now confirmed to remain open. The broader halo around the high-grade corridor returned 0.51 g/t gold over 118.16 metres, consistent with a Reduced Intrusion Related Gold System (RIRGS) geometry amenable to heap-leach bulk processing. Tectonic's 2026 drill program has completed over 22,000 metres year-to-date with assays pending from 97 additional holes — this is the first data wave of a very large dataset. A maiden Mineral Resource Estimate is targeted for Q1 2027. The 300-metre depth confirmation and RIRGS classification position Chicken Mountain as a potential bulk-tonnage, open-pittable gold target at scale in one of the last underdeveloped gold districts in North America. At $4,348+/oz gold, the heap-leach economics implied by a RIRGS system at this scale warrant serious attention from investors screening large Alaska gold land positions ahead of a maiden resource.

headline: GOLD ENDS WEEK AT $4,348, SILVER AT $64.39 — DOLLAR AND YIELDS DOMINATE HEADING INTO FOMC TUESDAY
snippet: Gold settled Friday September 11 at $4,348 per ounce — up 0.77% on the day but down roughly 0.3% for the week — while silver closed at $64.39, gaining 1.46% on Friday but losing approximately 4% on the week for its third consecutive weekly decline. Both metals logged weekly losses despite Friday's recovery from Thursday's PPI-driven selloff, as the combined August inflation data (PPI +5.4% annualized, core CPI +2.4% year-over-year) reinforced September 16 FOMC rate-hike expectations near 90% on CME FedWatch. The gold-silver ratio ticked up to approximately 67.5 — above the 50-year average near 60 — reflecting silver's disproportionate exposure to rate expectations through its industrial demand component. Rio Times' September 12 wrap frames the macro picture succinctly: the U.S. dollar and real Treasury yields are the dominant price drivers for gold and silver heading into FOMC week, with geopolitical factors absorbed rather than driving. For retail investors, the two price levels that matter most going into Tuesday's decision: $4,400 resistance on a hold or dovish signal would confirm the next leg of the 2026 bull; $4,200 support on a hike-plus-hawkish-dot-plot would signal a deeper correction phase. The gold price since the January 2026 record at $5,589 has traced a controlled correction — the September 16 decision will clarify whether that correction is done.
